findings: src/execution/perfect_aggregate_hashtable.cpp InitializeFusedUpdate: the eligibility conditions are general (count_star, sum_no_overflow over INT32/INT64, avg with a 16-byte AvgState<int64_t>, no filter, distinct or destructor). No names, literals or data properties are referenced.

The state layouts match: SumState<T>{bool isset; T value} (sum_helpers.hpp:27) and AvgState<T>{uint64_t count; T value} (avg.cpp:16). Static asserts and the runtime state_size check protect them. value=0 still comes from BaseSumOperation::Initialize, which is untouched.

Other avg variants are excluded correctly: TIMESTAMP/TIME avg uses AvgState<hugeint_t> (state size not 16), INT16 avg is rejected by physical type, and DOUBLE avg is rejected by input type. The INT32/INT64 int64-state avg only exists when avg.cpp:284 proves the sum cannot overflow, so overflow semantics are unchanged.

NULLs, constant vectors and dictionary vectors are handled through UnifiedVectorFormat sel/validity in the same way as the generic path (sum/avg skip NULLs, isset is set only on valid rows, count_star counts every row). The E0003 replica addressing is computed before FusedUpdate and the state offsets are built from payload_size, matching the existing AddInPlace loop.

Minor and not blocking: recognising functions by name could misfire for a user-registered aggregate named 'avg' with a 16-byte state and integer input. This is very unlikely, and the state_size check limits the risk.
